### Thread 1 — `CHANGELOG.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-11-13):
🚨 severity: BLOCKING —
🚨 **BLOCKING: This PR corrupts CHANGELOG.md with the exact CP1251 mojibake it exists to fix (305 lines, one byte irrecoverably lost)**

The commit that repairs mojibake decoding also **writes mojibake into the repo**: `CHANGELOG.md` was evidently opened on a CP1251 console/editor and re-saved — every multi-byte UTF-8 character whose bytes happen to be valid CP1251 was decoded as CP1251 and re-encoded as UTF-8. Verified byte-level on the branch (`sed -n '3p' CHANGELOG.md | hexdump` shows `d0 b2 d0 82` — the literal text is `вЂ"`, not `—`). `origin/main` has zero such lines; this branch has 305.

What got destroyed (all verified on the branch):

- **239× em-dash** `—` → `вЂ"` (e.g. `CHANGELOG.md:3`, `:9`, `:16`, `:1578`, `:1586`)
- **26× arrow** `→` → `в†'`, **9× `≤`/`≈`** → `в‰¤`/`в‰€`, **6× `«`/`»`** → `В«`/`В»`, **6× `·`** → `В·`, **4× `×`** → `Г—`, **2× `−`** → `в€'`, **1× `…`** → `вЂ¦`
- **`CHANGELOG.md:453`**: `⌘K/⌘3-9` → `вЊK/вЊ3-9` — `⌘` (U+2318, UTF-8 `E2 8C 98`) lost its trailing byte `0x98` (unassigned in CP1251), so this one is **not recoverable by a CP1251 round-trip** — real data loss, and a silent one: no test covers CHANGELOG content.
- **Even the new gh-2115 entry this PR adds is itself mojibaked**: `'Рї' arrives as the UTF-8 of 'ГЇ'` should read `'п' arrives as the UTF-8 of 'ï'`, and its two em-dashes are `вЂ"` (`CHANGELOG.md:171-182`).

This file is the **published artifact** — it ships on pub.dev (the file's own header documents the 262144-byte publish cap and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` exists precisely because pub.dev renders this file). Merging publishes ~300 corrupted changelog entries.

The fix is mechanical and fully recoverable from git:

```bash
git checkout origin/main -- CHANGELOG.md
# then re-add the gh-2115 entry under ## Unreleased as clean UTF-8
```

…and paste the new entry from a UTF-8-clean tool (the same mangling — `вЂ"` artifacts — is visible in the ticket/PR-description text too, so whatever editor/clipboard wrote it will re-corrupt it). A quick guard before committing: `grep -n 'вЂ\|в‰\|в†\|В«' CHANGELOG.md` must return nothing.

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/console_line_decoder.dart` line 89

**ai-teammate** (2026-11-13):
💡 severity: SUGGESTION —
💡 **SUGGESTION: structurally-complete invalid UTF-8 sequences still throw inside the new decoder — its own docstring says they surface as U+FFFD**

`ConsoleLineDecoder._decodeAt` classifies a sequence as `_SequenceShape.complete` on shape alone (right byte count, all continuations). But some *structurally complete* sequences are still invalid UTF-8, and the `complete` branch decodes them with strict `utf8.decode` (`console_line_decoder.dart:89`):

- overlong: `C0 80`
- encoded surrogate: `ED A0 80`
- > U+10FFFF: `F4 90 80 80`

`utf8.decode` throws `FormatException` on all three, and the exception propagates out of `convert` → errors the `lines` stream → the input line dies. That is precisely the gh-2115 symptom class, and it contradicts the file's own contract (line 24: "undecodable bytes surface as U+FFFD **instead of erroring**") and the PR description ("strictly more forgiving than the old `utf8.decoder` wiring").

Verified empirically against this branch (no hooks, the documented baseline):

```
overlong C0 80: THROWS FormatException: Invalid UTF-8 byte
surrogate ED A0 80: THROWS FormatException: Encoded surrogate
out-of-range F4 90 80 80: THROWS FormatException: Out of unicode range
```

No regression — the old `utf8.decoder` threw on these bytes too (verified in the same probe), and a human typing cannot produce them (they only arrive if a host/pipe feeds garbage into the ConPTY stdin the line REPL reads). So this is a contract-alignment issue, not a broken fix: `allowMalformed: true` closes the class —

```dart
case _SequenceShape.complete:
  out.write(_repairRun(utf8.decode(input.sublist(i, i + expected),
      allowMalformed: true)));
```

U+FFFD is outside the Latin-1 repair range, so the mojibake hook can never touch a replacement char, and the documented "never errors" guarantee becomes true for every byte value.

# pr-2116: fix(gh-2115): Russian input works in the Windows line REPL (code-page repair)

## Description

## What

Russian (and any non-ASCII) typing in the **fa line REPL on Windows** produced mojibake or killed the input line (gh-2115, follow-up to gh-1982 / gh-1973 which fixed the TUI only). This PR repairs the two wire shapes a legacy RU-locale console delivers:

| shape | wire for 'п' | old behavior | new behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| CP-6501 translation mojibake (ANSI byte re-encoded as a code point) | `C3 AF` (UTF-8 of 'ï') | composer shows `ïðèâåò` | composer shows `привет` |
| legacy OEM input page (ConPTY pipes, older consoles) | single byte `0xEF` | strict `utf8.decoder` throws → `FormatException` on the `lines` stream → input line dead | repaired via the console input page |

Measured byte-level with kernel32 FFI probes against a live ConPTY and a fresh console on RU-locale Windows 11 (cpIn=866, acp=1251). Under ConPTY pipes Dart's `stdin.hasTerminal` is false (`GetFileType` = pipe), so the TUI — which already guards its own path — never engages; the line REPL is the active surface, and it decoded stdin with a bare `utf8.decoder`.

## How

- **`ConsoleLineDecoder`** (`lib/src/cli/`, pure Dart, barrel-exported): streaming byte→line decoder with two injectable hooks — `runRepair` (repairs decoded Latin-1-range text through the ANSI code page) and `singleByteDecode` (decodes bytes no UTF-8 sequence could claim through the console input code page). True UTF-8 passes through untouched; undecodable bytes surface as U+FFFD instead of erroring the stream; partial sequences carry across stdin chunks; implemented via `startChunkedConversion` so `Stream.transform` works. With no hooks installed it is strictly more forgiving than the old `utf8.decoder` wiring and byte-identical otherwise.
